objective: Consequences of ticket A for the dictionary of BRACE-TREE: which rules reduce to finite spaces (atoms meeting at one cut, short chains) by the one-bit lemma and by the two-bit statement, with every reduced space checked exhaustively over its port permutations; which parts hold unconditionally (by the proved half) and which rest on the unproved part; and the source rule as a theorem as far as these reach.
status: Proved by TWO-BIT-SCREEN-20261105-001B-P001: in Fano trees (spaces built from Fano atoms alone), creation in the chain of atoms between two lines implies creation in the whole space, with equality when every atom off the path emits toward it; so every Fano atom is a block of mutual creation; the brace dictionary is one touching rule (a removal creates at a line of another atom exactly when that line touches its atom's cut toward the removal), which holds on all 294 two-atom and 576 three-atom gluings and on four-atom paths, and whose creating half holds in every Fano tree at distances one and two; non-creation holds in every chain and in four 25-point trees, and in general rests on the pendant-line statement
title: What screening gives the brace dictionary
